judged_text: The migration sets posts.cook_method default to 1, but Post.cook_methods Enum maps :regular to 0 and :raw_html to 1, so every existing and new post defaults to cook_method == raw_html. app/models/post.rb cook() returns raw for cook_method == :raw_html, so every normal post created after this migration skips the entire cooking/markdown/sanitization pipeline and is rendered as-is — all user-authored markdown breaks and unsanitized HTML is rendered site-wide.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1` and `Post.cook_methods ||= Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)` with `Post#cook` returning `raw` only for `:raw_html`. However, the finding’s core claim (that `Enum` maps `:regular` to 0 and `:raw_html` to 1, making the default effectively `:raw_html`) is not verifiable from this diff because the `Enum` implementation is not shown. In fact, existing code uses `Enum.new(:regular, :moderator_action)` for `Post.types`, and such enums in this codebase are commonly 1-based; the migration default of `1` strongly suggests it’s intended to mean `:regular`, not `:raw_html`.
